newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA IN TROUBLE AS RELATIONS SOUR.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA IN TROUBLE AS RELATIONS SOUR.

text.p: Australia sank into deep trouble in the fifth and final test against West Indies on Monday as relations between the two sides soured badly.
Umpires Peter Willey and Darrell Hair warned captains Mark Taylor and Courtney Walsh about persistent sledging.
Taylor completed a miserable morning when he was dismisssed for one as Australia battled to avoid an innings defeat on the third day at the WACA ground.
Needing to score 141 runs to make West Indies bat again, Australia were reeling on 32 for two at lunch after losing Taylor and number three Greg Blewett cheaply.
Opener Matthew Hayden was not out 14 in partnership with Mark Waugh, who remained unbeaten on nine.
Relations between the two camps deteriorated on Sunday when West Indies vice-captain and star batsman Brian Lara accused the Australians of persistent sledging.
When he was involved in another exchange during the morning session on Monday, the umpires stepped in.

"The umpires said there was a fair bit of niggle from both sides and that enough was enough," International Cricket Council match referee Raman Subba Row said in a statement released by the Australian Cricket Board.
"They called the two captains together and said it stops now or there shall be a report. It did stop and I am happy with that. There is no-one on report at this point," he said.
Lara, who scored his first century of the test series on Sunday, returned to the middle as a runner because of a hamstring injury to his captain and fast bowler Courtney Walsh.
Lara hurt his foot when he collided with Australia opener Matthew Hayden after completing a quick single, prompting an exchange of views between several players.
Umpire Hair spoke to Walsh and Taylor at length in the middle of the pitch before the two captains shook hands.

West Indies, who began the day on 353 for seven in reply to Australia's first innings 243, were dismissed for 384 before lunch. Carl Hooper failed to add to his overnight score of 57, while pace bowler Paul Reiffel claimed five for 73.
Taylor added another failure to a dismal run of recent scores when he edged a ball from fast bowler Curtly Ambrose to wicketkeeper Courtney Browne.
Australia's prospects of avoiding a crushing defeat appear slim given that the wicket is offering extremely variable bounce.
The poor condition of the wicket was illustrated when Ambrose bowled Blewett for a duck with a full-length delivery that barely lifted off the ground after pitching.
Australia have taken an unassailable 3-1 lead in the series to retain the Frank Worrell trophy.
